_readme: The human writing pass for the fractals tutorial. Merged over the auto-assembled skeleton by tools/build_critical_tutorial.py (apply_authored) — regeneration never clobbers this file. Voice: NOC directness + this project's critical reading. One idea per page; the renders carry the rest. R-009: walk hand-cut (mandelbrot_dive + box_counting_dimension promoted; recursive_tree_2 + fractal_scene stepped down — their prose kept below as visible orphans); Hilbert blank declared.

blanks.note: Space-filling curves are uncovered — the trunk runs from the int to the Hilbert curve and beyond, and the Hilbert curve has no plinth here. Candidates at depth: Hilbert3D, space_filling_curve_gallery. Declared open until ruled.

question.formula: D = log(N) / log(S)   ·   zₙ₊₁ = zₙ² + c
question.text: Hold a fern. The frond is made of fronds, and each of those is made of smaller fronds again — pull one leaflet off and you are holding a miniature of the thing you started with. Nature does this everywhere: coastlines, lungs, river deltas, broccoli. And it does it without a blueprint, because a blueprint would have to be as large as the thing itself. What nature has instead is a rule, applied again to its own output. This sequence is about what happens when a rule is allowed to see itself: shapes with infinite detail and finite bounds, dimensions that fall between the integers, forms that no amount of zooming will simplify. The formula above measures that in-betweenness. The rooms below let you stand inside it.

primitive.lead: Every sequence begins with one small thing that already contains the whole idea.

artifacts.fractal_recursion_2: One line of code: draw a square, then call yourself with half the size. That is the entire artifact — square(center, size, d) = box(size) + square(center, size·0.5, d−1) — and everything else in this sequence is already inside it. The function refers to itself, so the shape it draws contains itself; the stopping depth d is the only mercy keeping it finite. Stand close in VR: the smallest square is the whole artifact again, at a scale your headset can barely resolve. Recursion is not a technique here. It is the subject.

walk1.lead: Five artifacts, each one the previous idea pushed a step further — subdivision, selection, branching, self-reference, and recursion you can climb.

artifacts.recursive_table: Subdivision runs backwards too. Take a cube, cut it three by two, keep only the top layer and the four corners, flatten the top, stretch the legs — a table appears. Nothing was added at any point. The furniture was carved out of the possibility space, the way a sculptor insists the figure was always in the marble.
artifacts.recursive_chair: The same move with a different keep-list: three by three by three, keep legs, seat, back. Put the chair beside the table and the deeper claim becomes visible — these objects are not built, they are selected. One rule, different choices.
artifacts.inverted_tree_cloud: The first branching recursion, hung upside down. A trunk grows downward, branches shrink and scatter at random angles, a cloud of cubes orbits and fades. The inversion is the point: this is a root system — and the random angles quietly introduce the E in this sequence's formula, a deterministic rule with noise in its joints.
artifacts.fractal_scene: A whole room generated by the recursions you have just met, assembled at world scale — twenty-six metres deep. Walk it rather than look at it: it is the first artifact in the walk that is larger than your ability to see it all at once, which is precisely what infinite detail feels like from inside.
artifacts.example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr: Back to the pure form, in circles: a torus, then four half-size circles at its cardinal points, then sixteen, then more. This is the one to hold. It is small enough to grasp and deep enough to show the distinction that matters: a loop repeats an action, but this circle contains its own definition. Recursion is not repetition — it is self-reference.
artifacts.cube_staircase: Recursion along a diagonal: a tread, a riser, then call yourself one step down. It earns its place in the walk because it is recursion you can climb — the algorithm as architecture, load-bearing.
artifacts.fractal_scene: ORPHAN (stepped down from the walk, R-009 — prose kept): A whole room generated by the recursions you have just met, assembled at world scale — twenty-six metres deep. Walk it rather than look at it: it is the first artifact in the walk that is larger than your ability to see it all at once, which is precisely what infinite detail feels like from inside.

walk2.lead: Further in: ratio, choice, then the measure, the edge itself — and subtraction to close.

artifacts.recursive_tree_2: ORPHAN (stepped down from the walk, R-009 — prose kept): The canonical branching function, right side up this time: each branch spawns shorter, rotated copies of itself until the energy runs out. Every tree outside your window is this function with weather applied.
artifacts.box_counting_dimension: The instrument the whole chapter has been promising. Lay a grid over a shape and count the boxes it touches; halve the grid, count again; keep going. The exponent that emerges as the boxes shrink is D = log(N)/log(S) — the formula from page one, measured instead of asserted. A line's count doubles per halving; a plane's quadruples; a coastline lands stubbornly in between, and stays there at every ruler you can afford. Dimension stops being a given and becomes a reading — and like every reading in this book, it depends on the fineness of the instrument doing it.
artifacts.mandelbrot_dive: And then the edge itself. z → z² + c, iterated: for some c the orbit stays home forever, for others it flees to infinity, and the boundary between those two fates is the most complex object mathematics owns — infinitely detailed, nowhere smooth, and bounded. Dive: every magnification produces new coastline, seahorses, spirals, small copies of the whole set waiting at depths no one has visited. Here the chapter's QFEP claim stops being a metaphor. The Mandelbrot boundary IS the edge of chaos — order and entropy interlocked at every scale — and in this room you are not looking at it, you are falling along it.
artifacts.fibonacci_pagoda: Nine metres of golden ratio. Each tier is the one below divided by the root of φ, stacked up to a finial. From a distance it reads as architecture; up close it reads as pure number. That double reading is the sequence's quiet argument: culture and mathematics are not different materials.
artifacts.cube_subdivision: Eight children, keep one, recurse. Where the pagoda makes ratio visible, this makes choice visible: the path down the subdivision tree is a history of decisions, and the artifact is that history, frozen in place.
artifacts.example_8_4_cantor_set_vr: The walk ends with removal. Delete the middle third, then the middle of what remains, forever: infinitely many points, zero total length. The Cantor set closes the walk by inverting everything before it — the other artifacts built by adding smaller copies; this one builds by taking away.

turn.text: Every artifact in the walk holds its rule fixed and exposes its numbers. Depth is the honest knob — push it and cost explodes exponentially while new form arrives only logarithmically; that asymmetry is the fractal bargain, and every renderer pays it. The scale ratios (0.5, 0.7, 1/φ) set the personality of the whole; branch counts set density; random angles decide whether a form reads as mathematics or as biology. Open any of these in the dressing-room viewer and move one knob until the artifact stops being itself. The point where it stops is that parameter's real meaning.

critical.lead: Now the reading the renders have been implying all along.
critical.qfep_connection: Fractals embody the QFEP tension directly: F, the deterministic recursive rule, plus λE(S), random variation in the stochastic forms, makes shape at the edge of chaos. The Mandelbrot boundary is where order meets chaos — infinitely complex, yet bounded. And fractals are queer geometry in the precise sense: dimensionally non-normative, nowhere smooth, computationally irreducible — form that refuses the integer categories of line, plane and solid the way queer life refuses given categories, by existing fully, and permanently, in between.

world.lead: Ten rooms, and their order is the argument: first recursion held in the hand, then trees, then subtraction (Cantor), then the classical monsters (Koch, Sierpinski, Menger), then ratio (the golden spiral), then the edge of chaos itself (Julia, Mandelbrot), and finally a synthesis hall where they all stand together.
objectives: Self-similarity: the whole contains copies of itself
Fractal dimension: D = log(N)/log(S) — between the integers
Recursion as emergence: simple rules, infinite complexity
The edge of chaos: the Mandelbrot boundary, Julia variations

exercises: In Fractal_Recursion, find the deepest square you can actually see, then check how many levels the code claims exist. The difference between those two numbers is the gap between mathematics and rendering — write it down.
Open recursive_chair in the dressing-room viewer and change the keep-list in your head: which cells would you keep for a bench? A throne? Sketch the rule, not the object.
Walk Fractal_CantorSet and stand in one of the gaps. What was removed to make room for you? Answer in one sentence that uses the word 'creative'.
In Fractal_MandelbrotSet, try to point at the exact place where order ends and chaos begins. You will fail. Explain your failure using D = log(N)/log(S).
Take the pagoda's rule — divide by √φ per tier — and apply it to something that is not architecture: a schedule, a sentence, a family. Does it stay golden?
Compute the dimension of cube_subdivision's path: N = 1 kept, S = 2 scale, so D = 0. What does it mean that a history of choices has the dimension of a point?
seed.coda: The seed of this sequence fits in a sentence: a rule allowed to see itself makes infinite form from finite means. Carry it into L-systems, where the rule stops drawing and starts writing.

motifs.the measure: Dimension itself becomes a measurement — D = log(N)/log(S) lands between the integers, and the length of the ruler changes the coastline it measures.
motifs.the debt: Depth is the loan: each recursion level doubles what the render owes the ideal form while returning less new shape. The visible bottom of every fractal is a payment that stopped.
